## Accepted P09 review effect fixtures

The seven review cases use the existing ports and ordinary implementation paths. Retry fixtures first obtain a real camera busy or knock-404 response with retry_in, make the snapshot not ready and observe every holder/relay request before/at the monotonic deadline; local reads, turn renewal and neighbouring-console held reads remain available. The backup fixture supplies genuinely signed documents and matching checksums: each attempt independently starts from the same own pair; only the last attempt revokes the own issuer. Compare actual object/taken bytes after the smaller same-term pair is refused.

The key replacement fixture operates on real ring-protected seeds and the actual two store rows, loses the conditional-batch reply, and also presents a readable mismatched binding. Run the actual signing gate, operator-authorized maintenance execution by domainagent under its current turn guard, confirmation, normal holder re-admission and own-console signature check; no fabricated public-key decision or new operator command is introduced. Never return key/seed/signature bytes.

The member-want fixture drives ordinary part requests through two passes of the same process with eight real persistent 503 responses and a valid ninth part. Count actual requests, observe unchanged stored at values, completion/withdrawal cleanup and a real restart from the state after the first pass; restart restores the original persisted at/name order. The relay-age fixture executes real empty/other-member batches, forwards the real cached carry into the ordinary member copier/may age path, then receives a new carry for that same member and restarts. Its old cached grants are truly expired, not refreshed by global heard. The missing-cache fixture uses a genuine first empty-batch response admitting the member, then actual signed GET handlers; valid GET is 503 only after signature checking, invalid signature remains 401, and neither a knock nor an invented cached response is produced.

**Authorized local member-key replacement (P09 review C4).** This is an explicit operator-authorized maintenance procedure after loss or theft, not an agent's automatic response to an unreadable key. The operator must be authorized to replace this member identity and arrange normal re-admission of the new public key at the holder. Keep the pinned root/domain and cluster name unchanged. Stop all normal local agent instances and other member-key signers, wait for their old work to finish, and keep their automatic start disabled across interruption until the pair is confirmed. The operator invokes one local maintenance execution of the existing `domainagent` role with normal process-start admission and the active `domain/agent-turn`; it performs no ordinary reports or member signatures during maintenance. Open the authorized ring-protected replacement material, derive the new pub from its Ed25519 seed and seal the seed with the member ring. This agent writes `domain/member-key {seed_secret, pub}` and `domain/member {cluster, pub}` together in one ordinary conditional store batch by the confirmed versions of both rows and the current `domain/agent-turn` guard (N1.13). The operator authorizes and controls the window; the existing agent role is the writer, not a new role. No new public command spelling or HTTP route is prescribed.

If the write is interrupted or its outcome is unknown, signing and ordinary restart remain disabled, including while the agent resolves the ordinary turn/write unknown-outcome barrier. Confirm both rows by reading them again: both contain the authorized new matching pub and the seed derives it — the replacement is complete; both are the former pair — retry the authorized conditional batch under a confirmed current turn; a mixed, absent unexpectedly, unreadable or mismatched pair — repair through that same authorized agent procedure before continuing, never generate another seed automatically. Do not repair an unreadable existing key by the create-once path or merely copy a foreign pub into the key row. After the pair is confirmed, the active agent may sign its re-admission knock with the new key; normal reports require the holder's normal admission. Its own console verifies the new key from the updated `domain/member.pub`. At agent startup and before the agent signs, a readable existing binding with another pub or an unconfirmed binding blocks signing and uses the existing key_read/sign_failures path until repaired. Confirmed absence during the unchanged initial create-once/admission path is distinct and keeps that path; the procedure does not require a domain set before the first knock. No secret material is logged.

\n**Member-want queue lifetime (P09 review C5).** Keep retry ordering until the process ends, not only until the pass ends. Remove an entry when its request succeeds (`take` or `same`), is empty (404) or is withdrawn by its reader. Reconcile newly observed asks into the queue without resetting the order of pending retries. A completed request recreated later is a new entry; no stale cursor is reused. After restart only the persisted asks remain and their initial at/name order is rebuilt. This is bounded process memory, not a new durable row or a mutation of request `at`.\n

\n**Cached-carry origin (P09 review C1).** Store each cached carry together with its own receipt origin. Every response of that cached carry computes `domain_age` from that origin, including GET and the POST hold fallback. A successful empty batch, a carry for another member, retries and `heard` do not refresh it. A new carry of the same member replaces both its content and origin, even if its content compares equal; it is a genuinely new confirmed holder response. The relay cache, origins and `heard` are process memory: after restart there is no cached carry or inherited age until a new holder response supplies it. The receiving member retains its existing rule `as_of = receipt - domain_age`, with its freshness/write throttles; an old cache cannot renew expired grants.
